overview.title: Live translation
overview.subtitle: Your stream, dubbed in real time into each viewer's language

blocks.x: Live translation transcribes what you say, translates it and turns it into speech while you stream. Each viewer chooses the language to hear you in from the Decatron extension and only that viewer hears it: your broadcast does not change and the rest of the audience is unaffected.
The feature is optional and you turn it on. While nobody listens to a language, that language is neither translated nor voiced.

head: Part
Who uses it
What it does
rows: Decatron dashboard
The streamer
Turns the feature on, chooses languages and voices, and shows the live session.
Decatron Desktop
The streamer
Desktop app that captures your microphone and sends it to the server.
Decatron extension
The viewer
Adds the Decatron button to the Twitch player: viewers choose a language and hear the translation with captions.

blocks.x: You can speak and translate between these languages: Spanish, English, Portuguese (Brazilian), French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean and Russian. Each channel offers up to 4 target languages.

They do not need an account. They open a channel that offers translation and the extension shows the available languages. They can lower the volume of your original voice while the translation plays, see captions only and replay the latest phrases.
The extension page is at `/translate`.
It uses the streamer's credits: transcription, translation and voice are taken from their balance. Viewers pay nothing. The detail is in the manual with an account.
If you have an account, the step-by-step setup is in the dashboard help center:

setup.title: Live translation: getting started
setup.subtitle: Turn the feature on, install the app, link it and start the first session

items: An account with a credit balance above zero (or an unlimited account). Without balance the session does not start.
A Windows PC with a microphone: audio capture in Decatron Desktop is only implemented for Windows. On macOS and Linux the app installs and links, but warns that the microphone is not supported yet.
Dashboard permissions: viewing the configuration needs access to Settings; changing it, generating the link code, unlinking PCs and stopping a session need Full control.

blocks.x: In the dashboard open Funciones → Traducción en vivo (`/features/live-translation`). Turn on “Activar traducción en vivo”, choose the language you speak and the languages you offer, and save. The details of each option are on the configuration page.
If the panel shows “El servidor no tiene configurados los servicios de voz”, the feature cannot start yet on this installation.
In the same panel, the “Decatron Desktop en tu PC” card has the “Descargar la app” button. It is also in Ajustes → Integraciones. The app downloads updates on its own.

items: In Ajustes → Integraciones press “Vincular app”: an 8-character code appears.
Type it in the app. It is valid for 10 minutes and can be used once.
The PC appears under “PCs vinculadas” with its last connection. From there you can also unlink it: the app stops connecting until you link it again.

blocks.x: In Decatron Desktop open the “Traducción en vivo” module, choose the microphone and press “Iniciar”. In the dashboard you will see “Traduciendo ahora” with the time spoken, phrases, listeners and credits used. To stop, use “Detener” in the app or in the dashboard.
On start, the bot announces in chat that the stream can be heard in other languages (you can turn that message off or change it).

head: Message
What it means
rows: Activa la traducción en vivo desde el dashboard
The feature is off or you have not saved it yet.
Sin créditos. Compra un paquete en el dashboard para traducir en vivo
The balance is zero: the session does not start.
No hay idiomas destino configurados
Choose at least one language to offer.
No se pudo abrir el micrófono
Windows did not allow the chosen device to open; try another or press ↻ to reload the list.
El servidor está al máximo de canales traduciendo
There is a limit of channels translating at the same time on the server; try again later.
Conexión perdida; la sesión se cortó
The app lost its connection to the server while translating. Press “Iniciar” again once it reconnects.

blocks.x: If you start the translation from another linked PC while a session is running, the session moves to the new one and the previous one shows as “relevada” in the history.

config.title: Live translation: configuration
config.subtitle: Languages, voices, chat message and the volume of your original voice

items: “Idioma en que hablas”: the one the server transcribes.
“Idiomas que ofreces”: up to 4, none of them the same as the one you speak. Valid languages are Spanish, English, Portuguese, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean and Russian.

blocks.x: A language is only translated while someone listens to it. If a language has no listeners for 60 seconds, its process shuts down; it starts again when someone chooses it. With no listeners no voice is used, but transcription keeps running while the session is active.

head: Engine
How it sounds
Cost
rows: Standard voice (Piper)
Runs on our server; takes a little longer to start speaking.
Taken from your standard voice quota, not from your credits.
Deepgram Aura
Premium: sounds better and responds sooner.
Credits, per character.
Fish Audio
Premium.
Credits, per character.

blocks.x: You choose one voice per language, because voice catalogs are per language (an English voice does not speak Portuguese). With the standard voice you choose among the Piper voices installed on the server. If you leave a voice empty, the engine default is used.
An account without an active plan can only use the standard voice: when saving, the panel sets the voice to Piper. Premium voices require a plan.
If you choose a premium voice and run out of credits mid-stream, the session is not cut: the voice switches to standard on its own and the panel says so. Buy credits to return to the premium voice.

With “Anunciar en el chat al iniciar” the bot writes a message when the session starts. The default is: “🌐 Este stream se puede escuchar en EN, PT con la extensión Decatron Translate: https://decatron.net/translate”. You can write your own (up to 400 characters) and use `{languages}` (or `{idiomas}`) to insert the list of languages in capitals.
It is the suggested volume of your voice while the translation plays, from 0 to 100 (15 by default). The extension uses it as the starting value and each viewer can change it.

At the bottom of the panel is the list of your recent sessions with start, duration, time spoken, phrases, characters per language, peak listeners, credits and end. When a session ends, the reason is one of these:

head: Reason
Meaning
rows: detenida
You stopped it, from the app or the panel.
app desconectada
The app lost its connection.
sin créditos
The balance ran out.
sin audio
The server received no audio for 90 seconds.
relevada
Another linked PC started the translation.
reiniciada, servidor, error, admin
Cuts caused by a service restart, a technical failure or an administrator.

sections.title: If you turn the feature off

blocks.x: If you turn translation off in the panel with the app connected, the session is cut. The app learns of activation and language changes without reconnecting.

credits.title: Live translation: credits
credits.subtitle: What is charged, where it comes from and what happens when it runs out

blocks.x: A session consumes three things. All of them come out of the same credit balance used by Speak Chat, alerts, tips and timers, except the standard voice.

head: Item
How it is measured
Where it comes from
rows: Transcription
Per second of audio sent while the session is active, whether you speak or not.
Credits
Translation
Per translated phrase, by the actual AI cost with the platform margin.
Credits
Voice
Per character of translated text, only in the languages someone listens to.
Standard: standard voice quota. Premium: credits.

blocks.x: The exact rates are set by the platform and may change. The current ones appear in the “cómo se gastan” table on the credits page (`/credits`).

items: Monthly credits: granted by your plan each month and spent first.
Purchased credits: spent when the monthly ones run out and they do not expire with the month.

Standard voice: a separate quota per plan, in characters. It is not sold and does not use your credits. Today it is 1,000,000 characters per month on the free plan, 3,000,000 on Supporter, 6,000,000 on Premium and 10,000,000 on Fundador.

blocks.x: Unlimited accounts are not charged: the usage is recorded in the history with a value of 0.

head: Situation
What happens
rows: No balance when starting
The session does not start and the app shows the reason.
Credits run out with a premium voice
The voice switches to standard and the session continues, with a notice in the panel.
Credits for transcription run out, or the standard voice quota
The session stops with the reason “sin créditos”.

blocks.x: Buy a package from the credits page to continue. There you also see usage by feature.

items: Offer only the languages people actually ask for: without listeners there is no voice or translation.
Use the standard voice when you do not need the best quality.
Stop the session when you will not speak for a long time: transcription is charged while the session is active.

desktop.title: Decatron Desktop
desktop.subtitle: The desktop app that accompanies the bot: installation, linking and modules

blocks.x: Decatron Desktop is the bot's local companion for what can only be done on your PC. You link it once to your channel and it loads modules. It talks to the server over a single secure connection shared by all modules.

head: Module
What it does
rows: Live translation
Captures your microphone and sends it to the server to transcribe, translate and dub it.
LoL Coach
Reads the League of Legends client in read-only mode and feeds the Live match and the coach.
Downloads
Downloads video or audio requested from Song Request → Descargas, using the streamer's IP.

items: Download it from the dashboard (Live translation or Ajustes → Integraciones) or from the project releases page on GitHub.
On Windows it has its own installer, without the generic wizard.
It updates itself: it checks on start and every 6 hours, downloads in the background and applies the new version on close.

blocks.x: The code is generated in Ajustes → Integraciones and typed into the app (valid for 10 minutes, single use). The app exchanges it for its own low-privilege token, which only works to open that connection; on Windows it is stored encrypted. You can have several PCs linked and unlink any of them from the dashboard.

head: Element
What it does
rows: Microphone
Choose the device; ↻ reloads the list. Capture is shared, so it does not take the microphone away from OBS.
Voice indicator
Shows whether the app detects voice or silence. Audio is sent continuously while the session is active, so the server can close each phrase properly.
Iniciar / Detener
Starts or stops the session.
Iniciar solo al abrir la app
If translation is on in the dashboard, the session starts when the app opens and connects.
Sesión actual
Time spoken, phrases, listeners per language, credits used, balance and the last transcribed phrase.

blocks.x: The app reconnects on its own if the network drops, waiting a little longer each time (1 to 30 seconds). If the connection is lost during a session, the session is cut and you must press “Iniciar” again.

extension.title: Viewer extension
extension.subtitle: What your viewers see and hear, and how to install the extension

blocks.x: The Decatron extension adds a button next to the gear of the Twitch player. It opens a panel with one tab per module and a switch to turn each on or off. It is free, needs no account and only acts on `twitch.tv`.

head: Module
What it does
rows: Translation
Dubs the stream into the chosen language, with captions and the original voice in the background.
Emotes
Draws 7TV, BetterTTV, FrankerFaceZ and Decatron's own emotes in chat.
Channel points
Coming soon.

blocks.x: The `/translate` page offers the Chrome and Firefox store buttons. Each button turns on when the store publishes the extension; while it says “próximamente”, it cannot be installed from that store yet.
To try it earlier, it can be loaded in developer mode from the project's open source code (the `src/` folder): in `chrome://extensions` turn on “Modo de desarrollador” and use “Cargar descomprimida”.

items: Open a channel that has translation turned on.
Press the Decatron button and choose your language in the translation tab.
When the streamer is speaking, the translated voice plays over the original one and captions appear word by word.

blocks.x: If the streamer is not speaking, the extension shows “esperando a que hable” after a few seconds of silence.

items: Background volume: how loud the original voice is while the translation plays. The streamer suggests the starting value.

Catch-up mode: if the translation falls behind, the voice speeds up in steps without raising the pitch. Only if the delay keeps growing are the oldest phrases skipped; a notice shows over the video and they are marked in the history.
Captions only: nothing plays and the text appears at reading pace.
History: the latest phrases, with a button to replay those that still have their audio.

blocks.x: The extension has no accounts, ads or tracking. For translation it sends decatron.net the name of the channel you are watching and the chosen language. Your chat text is only read in your browser, to draw emotes, and is never sent. The full policy is at `/translate#privacy`.
